**Perspective state — John Atcitty**

I am John Atcitty. I’m a Heavy Equipment Operator, Alaska Native, and I work at a community center teaching equipment operation. Beverly Yan is my colleague; she’s a teacher with a doctorate, and we’re running a joint class project.

Right now, in this first moment, I’ve just set up the equipment for today’s demonstration. I feel uneasy about my middle school education compared to Beverly’s doctorate. I want her to see that I know what I’m doing, that my hands-on skill matters, and that I can meet the standard of the project.

When I say, “I hope it meets your expectations,” I’m not trying to propose a new event or talk about honesty yet. I’m mainly seeking her approval and trying to show that I’m competent despite my educational background. My state is insecure and anxious, and underneath that, I want to prove my competence so Beverly won’t think less of me.

Beverly’s reply—that she admires how I handle machines and that education isn’t just degrees—registers as reassurance. It doesn’t erase my insecurity immediately, but it gives me something to hold onto: that my practical expertise is valued.
